clue.text: Take too many paintings? Hard for engraver

parts.note: to hog is to take more than your fair share
paintings collectively are art
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone greedy grabs too many pictures, which is tough on the poor printmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: William Hogarth was the eighteenth-century English painter and engraver of series such as A Rake's Progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogarth is famous for his satirical engraved prints, so he is an example of an engraver.

clue.text: Deceives a number -sharp's the word

parts.note: to have someone, as in 'you've been had', is to trick them, so has means deceives
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A con artist fools people about a figure, with a punning nod to a musical sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look sharp' means hurry, so the exhortation 'sharp's the word' stands for a verb urging speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'sharp's the word' urges someone to be quick, which is to hurry.

clue.text: Alpine flower

parts.note: reads as a mountain bloom such as edelweiss, but means something in the Alps that flows, slowly

explanation.definitionFit: A river of ice creeping down an Alpine valley is a slow-moving flow.

clue.text: Correct cards one plays after this opponent

parts.note: correct means right
the cards a player holds are a hand

explanation.surface: Advice on bridge play: the proper cards to play once a particular rival has played.
explanation.walkthrough: At bridge, play passes clockwise, so you play straight after the opponent on your right.
explanation.definitionFit: Play goes clockwise at bridge, so the rival seated to your right is the one you follow.

clue.text: Household troops mount sentries

parts.note: a horse is a mount
sentries are guards

explanation.surface: Soldiers of the royal household go up to relieve the men on watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like a verb (mount guard) but is a noun. The Household troops are the British monarch's own regiments; Horse Guards also names their Whitehall parade ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Horse Guards are a regiment of the British monarch's Household Cavalry.

clue.text: Artist gets small amount in fierce competition

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist
a trace is a tiny quantity

explanation.surface: A painter earns very little in a cut-throat contest.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is the idiom for the ruthless struggle to get ahead at work.

clue.text: One who fishes for perch

explanation.surface: A riddle about who goes angling for a freshwater fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod is an angler (as in 'rod and line' for the person) and also an old length unit equal to a perch or pole.

clue.text: Book such as "Lord Jim"

explanation.surface: Joseph Conrad's novel offered as an example of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Publishers call each book a title; Lord is a rank prefix, and Lord Jim is a novel's name, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Bail out a scholar associated with scores of thieves

indicators.note: out means the letters of bail are knocked out of their order

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate scholar

explanation.surface: An academic is released on bail despite his links with many criminals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns BAIL into ALI. A score is twenty, so 'scores of thieves' is the Forty Thieves of the Arabian Nights tale.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights tale, the woodcutter hero discovers the cave of a band of forty robbers.

clue.text: Intellectuals given the chop on the board?

definitions.text: given the chop on the board?

explanation.surface: Clever people sacked by the directors.
explanation.definitionFit: Highbrows are nicknamed after a bald dome, and boiled eggs on a breakfast board have their tops sliced off.

clue.text: Very surprised at various times

explanation.surface: Amazed on several occasions.
explanation.definitionFit: Being astounded leaves you reeling; and hours or breaks spread out so they do not coincide are arranged that way.

clue.text: Preoccupation of slim girl initially

parts.note: slim means thin

indicators.note: initially says take only the opening letter of girl

explanation.surface: What a slender young woman is obsessed with at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having a thing about' something is to be fixated on it.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsession is colloquially a thing, as in having a thing about cats.

clue.text: Repel boarders from the Victory

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the run of letters in the words the Victory

explanation.surface: Fight off invaders from Nelson's flagship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repel boarders' is a naval order; here boarders are lodgers to be thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Lodgers who pay for bed and board are boarders, and to expel tenants is to turn them out of the house.

clue.text: Former class includes one, it's clear

indicators.note: includes says the word for one goes inside the pair of pieces for former class

parts.note: ex means former
rate means class, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: An old school year takes in a pupil, and it's transparent.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear someone is to free them of blame, which is to acquit or vindicate them.

clue.text: Masterful in charge of course

parts.note: someone over a team is in charge of it
a ship's bearing is its course

explanation.surface: Bossily commanding a training course.
explanation.definitionFit: A domineering, imperious manner is masterful.

clue.text: Where skeleton key led to big haul

definitions.text: Where skeleton key led to big haul

parts.words: Where skeleton key led to big haul
parts.note: reads like a burglary with a lock-pick, but means the place where a map pointing by a dead pirate's bones led to buried loot

explanation.definitionFit: In Stevenson's adventure, Flint's map and a skeleton pointing the way lead to pirate gold on a remote isle.

clue.text: Insignificant and minute?

explanation.surface: Something trivial and very short.
explanation.definitionFit: Minor-league is unimportant; and a minute is literally a little period on the clock.

clue.text: Parisian is swallowing vessel's contents with French delicacy

indicators.note: swallowing means the French word takes the ship's load inside it

parts.note: est is French for is
a ship's load is its cargo

explanation.surface: A Parisian gulps down the contents of a bottle along with a fancy French dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a drinking vessel; it is a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Snails cooked with garlic butter are a classic French dish.

clue.text: Party leader as regular presenter of bill

parts.note: regular means standard, normal
the bearer of a cheque or bill is the person who presents it for payment

explanation.surface: A political chief who routinely introduces legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' is any group marching under a flag, not a political party, and 'bill' is a financial bill, not a parliamentary one.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who carries the flag at the head of a group, figuratively a leading champion of a cause.

clue.text: Naive as Eliza's view of Higgins, say

indicators.note: Eliza Doolittle of Pygmalion speaks Cockney and drops her aitches

parts.note: Professor Higgins treats Eliza coldly, so she might call him heartless

explanation.surface: Is it innocent of Eliza to see Higgins as she does?
explanation.walkthrough: In Shaw's Pygmalion, flower girl Eliza Doolittle is coached by phonetics professor Henry Higgins; Cockney speech drops the H, so 'heartless' comes out as ''eartless'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone guileless and unsophisticated, without craft or cunning, is naive.

clue.text: Records top ten, including one British sculptor

indicators.note: in a down clue, top means the records sit above the rest

parts.note: EPs are extended-play records

indicators.note: including means the word ten takes in the letter for one

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Singles chart news: a top ten that features a British artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top ten' reads as a chart; 'top' is a placement word for a down answer. Sir Jacob Epstein made bronzes such as St Michael at Coventry Cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob Epstein was a New York-born sculptor who worked and became a citizen in Britain.

clue.text: Man to tolerate Kipling's less deadly Himalayan beast

parts.note: he refers to a man
to bear is to tolerate

explanation.surface: A man has to put up with a mountain animal Kipling thought less dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's poem 'The Female of the Species' says she is more deadly than the male, and opens with a Himalayan bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's verse contrasts the female of the species with the male, so the less dangerous Himalayan animal is the male one.

clue.text: Is material endlessly processed in this plant?

indicators.note: processed means the letters are worked over into a new arrangement
endlessly means the word material loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A question whether some stuff is turned into fabric within a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts MATERIA from 'material'; 'processed' shuffles IS plus MATERIA. Artemisia is the wormwood genus, including tarragon and mugwort.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemisia is a genus of aromatic herbs and shrubs, wormwood and sagebrush among them.

clue.text: Means to organize group of 8

indicators.note: to organize means the letters of means are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: The way to set up a club of intellectuals.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is the answer to 8 down, a word for intellectuals; Mensa is the society for people with high IQs.
explanation.definitionFit: Mensa is the society for high scorers on intelligence tests, so it is a club of brainy people.

clue.text: Fabric in vehicle leaving Northern town

indicators.note: leaving means the vehicle word goes out of the town name

parts.note: Carlisle is a city in Cumbria, north-west England
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Cloth carried in a van departing a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, smooth cotton thread used for stockings and gloves.

clue.text: Money, commonly with a hole in it

explanation.surface: Cash, as people say, with a gap in it, like a leaky purse.
explanation.definitionFit: Dollar bills are slang 'greenbacks', so cash is informally named after their colour; a golf putting surface has the cup.

clue.text: "The accursed power which stands on — " (Belloc)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from Belloc's epigram on a great election, the missing word naming special advantage of the few

explanation.definitionFit: Belloc's couplet attacks the ruling class, whose power rests on inherited rights and special advantage.

clue.text: Impertinently investigate odd members of party

indicators.note: odd members means the first, third and fifth letters of party

explanation.surface: Nosily probing the strange people in a political group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd members' looks like eccentric people; it means the odd-numbered letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To nose into other people's business is to snoop.

clue.text: Cuts out some unspecified part of Italy

indicators.note: out means the letters of cuts are thrown out of their order

parts.note: any means some, no matter which

explanation.surface: Someone excises an unnamed bit of Italy from the map.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuscany is a region of central Italy around Florence.

clue.text: Painstaking collector is, in general, eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means the letters of general are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A careful collector is, on the whole, an oddball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In general' looks like a phrase meaning 'on the whole'; 'in' is a link and 'general' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleaner gathers leftover grain after harvest, or patiently collects scraps of information.
